pr_body:
This PR applies @ashmaroli's kramdown v2 upgrade to the Jekyll 3.x series.

Ultimately I would like to be able to support both versions, but that may not be viable.

Upgrading to kramdown v2 requires bundling extra extension gems, so that is a consideration for GitHub Pages and other hosting sites that curate a list of dependencies.

/cc @jekyll/core 

Fixes #8315

issue_context.title: Kramdown v2 support for Jekyll v3.x
issue_context.body:
## Summary

I'd like to upgrade to kramdown v2 in GitHub-pages but we're blocked by the hard requirement that Jekyll v3.8.7 has on kramdown v1.

## Motivation

kramdown v2.3.0 has a CVE fix that we'd like to ship.

## Guide-level explanation

- [x] Ship kramdown v2 support to the 3.9-stable branch (prior art: https://github.com/jekyll/jekyll/pull/7492) https://github.com/jekyll/jekyll/pull/8322
- [ ] Release Jekyll v3.9.0 with kramdown v2 support

## Drawbacks

This further makes the move to Jekyll v4 less appealing and diverts efforts to this older version of Jekyll. That said, GitHub Pages is blocked upgrading to Jekyll v4 due to "invisible" breaking changes that would cause confusion and frustration for Pages users.

/cc @jekyll/core
comments:
kramdown v2 drops core bundling of various converters and parsers in favor of their namesake kramdown extensions.
Is GitHub Pages willing to bundle those gems as well to maintain backwards-compatibility?
Yep! Our key approach is to ensure the user experience is as unchanged as possible from today to tomorrow (except for pure enhancements of course 😄 ).
Apart from the above *minor hiccup*, relaxing the version constraint from `kramdown ~> 1.14` to `kramdown >= 1.14 < 3.0` shouldn't pose an issue for users still on the Jekyll 3.x train.
